questions.stem: Why do atoms form chemical bonds?

options.text: To increase their number of protons
To achieve a stable electron arrangement, usually a full outer shell

questions.explanation: Atoms form chemical bonds to achieve a stable electron arrangement, typically a full outer shell like the noble gases. This makes the atoms more stable.

questions.stem: What type of bonding occurs between a metal and a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Ionic bonding occurs between metals and non-metals. The metal atom transfers electrons to the non-metal atom, forming positive and negative ions that attract each other.

questions.stem: What type of bonding occurs between two non-metal atoms?
questions.explanation: Covalent bonding occurs between non-metal atoms. The atoms share pairs of electrons so that both atoms achieve a full outer shell.

questions.stem: Which type of bonding involves a 'sea' of delocalised electrons?
questions.explanation: Metallic bonding involves a lattice of positive metal ions surrounded by a 'sea' of delocalised electrons. These shared electrons hold the metal ions together.

questions.stem: In ionic bonding, what happens to the electrons?

options.text: Electrons are transferred from one atom to another
Electrons are delocalised throughout the structure

questions.explanation: In ionic bonding, electrons are transferred from the metal atom to the non-metal atom. The metal loses electrons to form a positive ion, and the non-metal gains electrons to form a negative ion.

questions.stem: Which group of elements rarely forms bonds with other atoms?
questions.explanation: Noble gases (Group 0) already have full outer electron shells, so they are very stable and have little tendency to form bonds with other atoms.

questions.stem: What is the main force that holds ions together in an ionic compound?

options.text: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions

questions.explanation: Ionic bonds are strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions. The positive ions (cations) and negative ions (anions) are held together by these forces.
